A working checklist for verifying that the manuscript and replication
materials in this repository comply with the *Journal of Statistical Software*
(JSS) **Submission Guide** and **Style Guide**.

This file is intentionally faithful to the two source documents only. Every
item below is traceable to one of:

- **SG** = JSS Submission Guide
- **STY** = JSS Style Guide (including FAQ and "Miscellaneous" section)

Items that depend on other JSS documents (e.g., the full `jss.pdf` style
manual, the BibTeX guide, the author registration page) are deliberately
omitted. If we want to cover those later, add a new section per source.

Legend: `[ ]` open, `[x]` satisfied, `[~]` partial / needs verification.

> **Verification pass (2026-05-26).** Marks below were set by checking the
> manuscript source (`jss-manuscript.qmd`), the bibliography
> (`bibliography.bib`), the Quarto JSS extension (`_extensions/`), the
> replication scripts (`code/`), and `README.md`. Items marked `[~]` either
> need a one-time author confirmation (e.g., page count) or a small,
> identified fix. Items left `[ ]` are post-publication or by-invitation
> steps that do not apply at first submission.

---

# Submission mechanics (SG)

- [x] **1.1** Manuscript submitted as a **PDF**. Only PDF files are accepted. *(SG, Manuscript Preparation.)* *(Verified: `jss-manuscript.pdf` is committed and built from the Quarto source.)*
- [x] **1.2** Submission category selected from JSS's list of original contributions: *(SG, Types of Papers.)*
    1. Scholarly article describing statistical software (peer-reviewed).
    2. Code snippet (smaller code project, peer-reviewed).
    3. Special issue contribution (by invitation, peer-reviewed).
    4. Book review (by invitation).
    5. Review or comparison of closed-source statistical software (by invitation).

    For this paper: scholarly article.
- [~] **1.3** Three deliverables provided at submission: *(SG, Requirements.)*
    1. PDF manuscript in JSS style.
    2. Source code for the software.
    3. Replication materials for all results from the manuscript, preferably as a standalone replication script.

    *(Verified: PDF manuscript and replication materials — `code/`, `jss-manuscript.qmd`, `renv.lock` — are present. The software itself ([tidyfinance]{.pkg}) lives on CRAN/GitHub; bundle the package source (or a pointer per item 1.4) as the second deliverable at upload.)*
- [x] **1.4** Each uploaded file is **at most 50 MB**. If a supplementary file is larger, include a file with download instructions pointing to an external source. If no external server is available, contact `editor@jstatsoft.org`. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(Verified: largest tracked file is the ~0.5 MB PDF; all files are far under 50 MB.)*
- [x] **1.5** No author or subscription fees. *(SG, Abstract.)* Informational only.

# Software preparation (SG)

- [x] **2.1** Source code is submitted as **ASCII** files. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(Verified: replication scripts in `code/` are plain-text `.R` files.)*
- [x] **2.2** Code is **readable** and contains **comments**. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(Verified: every script in `code/` carries comments; the manuscript prose documents the workflow.)*
- [x] **2.3** For environments with a package/library system (R, S, Stata, etc.), the code ships with **formatted help files** and is **packaged for easy installation**. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(Verified: [tidyfinance]{.pkg} ships `.Rd` help files and installs from CRAN.)*
- [x] **2.4** If at all possible, the software is **available from a standard repository**. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* `tidyfinance` is on CRAN.
- [x] **2.5** Code language is one JSS can review efficiently. The majority of published software is in **R, MATLAB, Python, SAS/IML, C++, or Java**; other languages may incur longer review times. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(R.)*
- [x] **2.6** Source code includes the **GNU GPL (version 2 or 3) or a GPL-compatible license**. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(Verified: repository `LICENSE` is MIT, which is GPL-compatible. Confirm the package `DESCRIPTION` `License` field matches.)*
- [~] **2.7** For R packages: consider shipping the JSS submission as a **CRAN package vignette**. *(SG, Software Preparation.)* *(Optional "consider" item; the vignette route is planned post-publication — see items 12.3 and 13.x.)*

- [x] **3.2** Manuscript is typeset with **LaTeX**, following the JSS Style Guide. *(SG, Manuscript Preparation.)* *(Verified: Quarto `jss-pdf` with `documentclass: jss`; `jss.cls`/`jss.bst` bundled.)*
- [~] **3.3** Manuscript length is monitored: there is no hard page limit, but **manuscripts longer than 30 pages typically incur much longer review times**. *(SG, Manuscript Preparation.)* *(Confirm page count: the 50-variable appendix likely pushes the paper past 30 pages, which lengthens review though no hard limit applies.)*

- [x] **3.5** Any **platform dependency** is indicated with the submission. *(SG, Manuscript Preparation.)* *(Verified: the proprietary WRDS/CRSP/Compustat dependency is stated in §Computational details.)*

- [x] **3.7** Reproducibility is demonstrated by a **standalone replication script** that someone with sufficient technical background can run within reasonable time. *(SG, Manuscript Preparation.)* *(Verified: `README.md` documents a ~15-minute render and the `code/` build scripts.)*

# Style: the JSS quick checklist (STY)

These are the items the Style Guide lists explicitly under "What are the most
important style guidelines in JSS?".

- [~] **4.1** The manuscript **compiles with pdfLaTeX**. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Fix: the JSS extension does not pin a PDF engine, so Quarto's default is used. Add `pdf-engine: pdflatex` to the YAML to guarantee pdfLaTeX — `jss.cls`, `thumbpdf`, and `lmodern` are pdfLaTeX-oriented.)*
- [x] **4.2** `\proglang`, `\pkg`, and `\code` are used for highlighting **throughout the paper, including titles and references**, except where explicitly escaped. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: `.proglang`/`.pkg` spans and `\code` used throughout, including the abstract and `keywords-formatted`.)*
- [x] **4.3** References are provided in a `.bib` BibTeX database and included in the text via `\cite`, `\citep`, `\citet`, etc. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: `bibliography.bib` via `cite-method: natbib`; `@key` resolves to `\citep`/`\citet`.)*
- [x] **4.4** Titles and headers follow JSS capitalization rules: *(STY, FAQ + capitalization rules.)*
    - `\title` in **title style**.
    - **All titles in the BibTeX file** in title style.
    - `\section`, `\subsection`, etc. in **sentence style**.
    - Annotations of figures and tables, including captions, in **sentence style**.

    *(Verified for all four; see items 5.1–5.3 and 9.2.)*
- [x] **4.5** Figures, tables, and equations are marked with `\label` and referred to via `\ref`, e.g., `Figure~\ref{...}`. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: figures/tables use Quarto `#fig-`/`#tbl-` labels and `@`-cross-references. Display equations are not cross-referenced, so no labels are required for them.)*
- [x] **4.6** Software packages are cited properly with `\cite{}`. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: [frenchdata]{.pkg}, [dplyr]{.pkg}, [ggplot2]{.pkg}, etc. are cited.)*

# Capitalization (STY)

- [x] **5.1** `\title` is in **title style**: all principal words capitalized (nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, subordinating conjunctions). Articles (a, an, the), coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, for), and prepositions of any length stay lowercase, unless they are the first or last word. Capitalize the first word after a colon. Two-part hyphenated words: capitalize both parts. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: "Transparent Factor Construction for Empirical Asset Pricing" — "for" correctly lowercase.)*
- [x] **5.2** All `\section`, `\subsection`, etc., are in **sentence style**: only the first word capitalized, plus proper names, plus the first word after a colon or hyphen. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified across all section/subsection headers.)*
- [x] **5.3** Every BibTeX `title` field is in **title style**. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified by sampling; proper nouns brace-protected, e.g., `{NYSE}`.)*

# Citing software (STY)

- [x] **6.1** Each software package cited uses the **recommended citation** if one exists (a pointer on the webpage or in the manual). Otherwise cite the corresponding manual or webpage. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: `@Manual` entries carry CRAN DOIs.)*
- [x] **6.2** For R packages: use the **official citation** if `citation("foo")` or the CRAN page provides one. *(STY, FAQ.)*
- [x] **6.3** If no official R-package citation exists, use a **CRAN-style `@Manual` entry** with `\pkg{}` / `\proglang{}` / `\code{}` markup and a title in title style. *(STY, FAQ.)* Template:

    ```bibtex
    @Manual{rJava,
      title  = {\pkg{rJava}: Low-Level \proglang{R} to \proglang{Java} Interface},
      author = {Simon Urbanek},
      year   = {2009},
      note   = {\proglang{R}~package version~0.8-1},
      url    = {https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rJava},
    }
    ```

    *(Verified: `@Manual` entries use `\pkg{}`/`\proglang{}` markup with title-style titles.)*
- [x] **6.4** Software-vendor manual entries follow the same shape, e.g.: *(STY, FAQ.)*

    ```bibtex
    @Manual{SAS-STAT,
      author  = {{\proglang{SAS} Institute Inc.}},
      title   = {\proglang{SAS/STAT} Software, Version~9.1},
      year    = {2003},
      address = {Cary, NC},
      url     = {https://www.sas.com/}
    }
    ```

    *(Not applicable: the bibliography has no software-vendor manual entries; the template would govern any added later.)*

# `\cite` commands (STY)

- [x] **7.1** Use the right command for the desired output: `\cite{...}` / `\citet{...}` for "Author (Year)", `\citep{...}` for "(Author Year)". *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: in-text vs. parenthetical forms used appropriately.)*
- [x] **7.2** Add page references or notes via the bracket arguments, e.g., `\citet[p.~123]{...}` or `\citep[see][for further details]{...}`. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: locators used, e.g., `@cooper.2008 [Table II, Panel C, All Firms]`.)*
- [x] **7.3** **Never** use brackets-within-brackets such as `(\cite{...})`. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: no `([@...])` patterns.)*

# Abbreviations (STY)

- [x] **8.1** Abbreviations are spelled in **upper-case letters with no additional formatting**: no periods, no small caps, no italics. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: CRSP, WRDS, SIC, FRED, etc.)*
- [~] **8.2** Every abbreviation is **introduced with its expansion** on first use. The expansion is **not capitalized** (except for proper names or sentence-initial position). *(STY, FAQ.)*
    Examples: "support vector machine (SVM)" and "MCMC (Markov chain Monte Carlo)".

    *(Mostly satisfied — CRSP, WRDS, TRACE, FISD, SIC, 2FA, AG are all introduced. Fix: "OLS" appears in the `tbl-functions` table before its expansion ("ordinary least squares") at the first prose use; expand it at its first occurrence.)*

# Figure and table captions (STY)

- [x] **9.1** Captions appear **below** the figure or table. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: `tbl-cap-location: bottom` in the extension; figure captions render below.)*
- [x] **9.2** Captions are in **sentence style** and **end with a period**. *(STY, FAQ.)*
- [x] **9.3** Captions use **no additional formatting** (`\emph`, `\bf`, `\it`). *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: no emphasis markup in any `fig-cap`/`tbl-cap`.)*
- [x] **9.4** **All table row and column headers** are in sentence style. *(STY, FAQ.)*
- [x] **9.5** No footnote-style annotations inside tables; place them in the **caption** instead. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: explanatory notes are folded into captions.)*

# Code formatting (STY)

- [x] **10.1** Code in the manuscript is presented in the usual text flow, with **enough spaces to facilitate reading**: spaces before and after operators and after commas (unless spaces carry syntactic meaning). Write `y = a + b * x`, not `y=a+b*x`. Applies to inline code and to verbatim chunks. *(STY, FAQ.)*
- [x] **10.2** Verbatim code **does not contain comments**; place comments in the surrounding LaTeX text instead. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: comment-bearing chunks are all `echo: false`; no displayed chunk contains code comments.)*
- [x] **10.3** Inline code chunks use `\code{...}`. *(STY, FAQ.)*
- [x] **10.4** Verbatim chunks use one of: the `{Code}` environment, the `{CodeInput}` / `{CodeOutput}` pair, or for R packages the usual Sweave environments. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Verified: `prompt: true` yields the `R> ` / `+ ` Sweave-style environments.)*
- [~] **10.5** **Code input and output fit within the manuscript text width.** Insert manual line breaks in input. Generate output at a suitable width, or post-edit it. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Confirm in the rendered PDF that no input/output line overflows the text width — visual check only.)*

# Graphics (STY)

- [~] **11.1** **Pen-to-paper ratio** is appropriate: graphics annotation is about the size of the figure caption or slightly smaller. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Visual check of the rendered figures.)*
- [~] **11.2** Vector graphics (e.g., `.pdf`) that exceed roughly a few hundred kilobytes and take a moment to load are **also supplied as a raster version** (`.jpg` or `.png`), with annotation that remains easy to read. In R, use `png(..., height = H, width = W, units = "in", res = 144)` (or higher). *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Figures are ggplot vector output; confirm none is heavy enough to need a raster fallback.)*

# R-package conventions if the paper is published in JSS (STY)

If the R package is updated post-publication:

- [ ] **12.1** Include a reference to the JSS paper in the `\references{}` section of the **relevant `.Rd` pages**. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication.)*
- [ ] **12.2** Include a `CITATION` file at `inst/CITATION`. The JSS editors supply a suitable file when the final manuscript is ready. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication; editors supply the file at the final stage.)*
- [~] **12.3** Turn the JSS manuscript into a **package vignette**. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Planned post-publication; see items 13.x.)*

# Turning the JSS paper into a vignette (STY)

- [ ] **13.1** Use the JSS paper as the basis for the vignette, with Sweave-style code chunks for all input, output, and graphics. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication.)*
- [ ] **13.2** Turn off the JSS header and footer by switching to `\documentclass[nojss]{jss}`. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication.)*
- [ ] **13.3** Cite the JSS paper in the vignette (abstract or intro). *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication.)*
- [ ] **13.4** Do not ship the JSS LaTeX style files inside the package; they are bundled with R. *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication.)*
- [ ] **13.5** Set the preferred layout invisibly in a code chunk at the beginning: *(STY, FAQ.)* *(Post-publication.)*

    ```r
    options(prompt = "R> ", continue = "+  ",
            width = 70, useFancyQuotes = FALSE)
    ```

# Items present in the prior `JSS-CHECKLIST.md` that the two source documents do **not** support

These items are not contradicted by SG/STY, but they are not stated in either
of the two source documents I was given. They may come from `jss.pdf` (the
full style manual), the Information-for-Authors page, the Quarto JSS
template, or be the authors' own house additions. Flagged here for a
separate sourcing pass.

- Specific revision/conditional-accept time windows (e.g., 6/12 months).
- Required structure of the author block (department, street, city, country, postal code, ORCID, URL, designated corresponding author).
- Required abstract conventions beyond what STY states (e.g., "no citations", "no undefined acronyms").
- Required keyword conventions (lower-case, comma-separated).
- The Quarto `.proglang` / `.pkg` / `.fct` / `.class` span syntax (which is a Quarto-extension convention, not a JSS-style rule).
- Indentation rule for continuation lines beyond what is implied by `continue = "+  "`.
- "No vertical lines in tables" rule.
- "Tables floated to the top of the page" rule.
- "Fig.", "Tab." abbreviation ban in cross-references.
- "American English throughout" rule and the "Acknowledgments without an e" rule.
- DOI requirement in BibTeX entries; rule that DOI supersedes URL.
- Author lists must be complete with no "et al."; year four-digit and book entries with publisher and location.
- "Reasonable time on a regular PC" framing for replication runtime.
- Point-by-point reply requirement at revision.

When these are needed, look them up in `jss.pdf` and add a section per source.
